claims.statement: The offline verification entry point is `npm test`, which runs `vitest run` with no vitest configuration file in `app/`; the specs live under `app/tests/**` and import the TypeScript sources under `src/` directly, so the suite needs neither a build nor Electron and never exercises `dist/`.

Specs are type-checked but never compiled into the build: `tsconfig.typecheck.json` includes `src/**` and `tests/**` with `noEmit`, while the emit configuration includes only `src/main`, `src/preload` and `src/shared`.

No module loaded by the offline suite may import `electron` at module scope: `kernel.ts` guarantees it (it builds the clock snapshot inline so the file stays loadable in plain Node, stated in the comment above `dataplaneSnapshot`), and `panel-kernel.ts` documents the converse that its own `DataplaneService` import is the Electron-only exception no offline test may load.

The deliberate exception to the no-electron-import rule is `src/main/services/dataplane.ts`, a cordis service class under `services/` whose first line imports `utilityProcess` from electron; it is registered only by `createPanelKernel`, and the offline suite instead binds `LocalPanelDataService` as the second implementation of the `PanelDataPort` seam.

`createKernel` registers `LocalPanelDataService` before `BridgeService` because the bridge declares an inject list that requires `panelData`, so assembly order — not just the plugin set — is part of what the kernel-level tests depend on.

Electron and native code become reachable only through lazily bound adapters with pure-Node fallbacks, which is what makes importing them under plain Node harmless: `desktop/adapter.ts` binds `koffi` and resolves `require('electron')` inside individual functions and falls back to `homedir()/Desktop` when `app.getPath` is unavailable, `focus/adapter.ts` and `usage/native.ts` bind their DLLs on first use, and `paths.ts` falls back from `app.getPath('userData')` to `LOCALAPPDATA`.

Every collector exposes its external world as an interface and accepts a `Partial` override in its options, with missing entries filled from the real source using `??`; tests therefore inject only the parts they care about and keep the real pure-Node implementations for the rest, and the suite uses no module mocking.

`HardwareService`'s injected interface is `HardwareSources` (`cpuTimes`, `memory`, `net`, `gpu`, `monotonic`) defined in `src/main/services/hardware.ts`, and its real source is `systemHardwareSources()` in the same file: `os.cpus`/`os.totalmem`/`os.freemem`, a lazily required `net-counters` reader, a `GpuQuery` over `nvidia-smi` with a 5 s TTL, and `performance.now()/1000` as the monotonic clock.

`DesktopService`'s injected interface is `DesktopDeps` (`listDir`, `extractIcon`, `open`, `watch`, `readShortcutTarget`, `fileExists`, `readStoreText`, `writeStoreText`, `iconScores`) defined in `src/main/services/desktop.ts`, with real sources in `src/main/desktop/adapter.ts`; `extractIcon: null` is a supported mode that disables the icon face (used by the data-plane assembly, where `app.getFileIcon` is unavailable).

`UsageService`'s injected interface is `UsageDeps` (`runningPidExes`, `foregroundExe`, `readPrior`) defined in `src/main/services/usage.ts`, whose real sources are `nativeRunningPidExes`/`nativeForegroundExe` in `src/main/usage/native.ts` and `readUserAssistPrior` in `src/main/usage/userassist.ts`; the log directory is a separate injectable knob so tests always point it at a temporary path.

`SearchService`'s injected interface is `SearchDeps` (`search`, `open`, `reveal`, `now`) defined in `src/main/services/search.ts`, whose real sources are `listarySearch` from `src/main/search/client.ts`, `shellOpen`, a `spawn('explorer', ['/select,', path])` reveal and `performance.now`; the injectable clock is what makes debounce and backoff timing testable, and port/limit are separate options.

`FocusService`'s injected interface is `FocusDeps` (`listWindows`, `focusWindow`, `launch`, `env`) defined in `src/main/services/focus.ts`, whose real sources are `nativeWindowCandidates`/`nativeFocusWindow`/`shellLaunch` in `src/main/focus/adapter.ts` and `process.env`; the tool→exe mapping (`Options.tools`) is a separate injectable knob that tests replace with a one-entry fake.

`SessionsService` is the one collector without a dependency bundle: its seam is the injectable roots map `SessionRoots` (one directory per tool), whose real value comes from `defaultSessionRoots()` derived from `os.homedir()`.

Every periodic loop in `createKernel` has a zero switch documented as "0 = no timer, the offline test drives it by hand": `tickIntervalMs`, `hardwareIntervalMs`, `usageIntervalMs` and `searchIntervalMs`. Kernel-level specs set them to 0 and call `ctx.bridge.tick()`, `ctx.hardware.sample()`, `ctx.usage.collect()` and `ctx.search.tick()` instead; a side effect is that the hourly `USAGE_PRUNE_MS` prune is only installed together with the usage poll timer.

`createDataplaneKernel` is the subprocess-side assembly: the same four collectors (sessions, hardware, usage, desktop) with their own timers and an `onSnapshot` out-port, and no bridge, search, settings, focus or plugin services; its spec runs it with 10 ms real intervals plus a 60 ms wait and asserts the snapshot shape and the desktop write path, while the `parentPort` glue in `src/main/dataplane.ts` is deliberately left to the acceptance battery.

Across the process boundary the same dependency slot is satisfied by an RPC proxy: the data plane is given `readShortcutTarget: (lnk) => resolver.resolve(lnk)` where `resolver` is `ProxyShortcutResolver`, which batches unresolved paths to the panel process over the protocol, caches negative results and suppresses in-flight duplicates; the proxy is verified offline as pure logic by injecting a fake sender.

`tests/contract.spec.ts` is the executable form of the renderer API: it boots the in-process kernel and drives `ctx.bridge.invoke(method, payload)` and `ctx.bridge.subscribe(event, listener)` for the method and event tables declared in `src/shared/contract.ts`, pinning the snapshot sections, push-on-tick and unsubscribe semantics, and the `BridgeError` rejection for an unknown method.

The contract suite pins response conventions rather than just shapes: user-facing actions degrade with `{ok: false, action: 'degraded'}` (and the panel keeps answering `panel/snapshot`) instead of throwing, `settings/set-card-opacity` clamps finite values and rejects non-finite ones, and guardrails keep `desktop/launch` inside the current scan pool, `search/action` inside the most recent result set, and `session/focus` to own properties of `config.tools`.

The IPC transport is not covered by any offline spec: `wireBridgeIpc`'s `ok`/`error` envelope, its fixed `FORWARDED_EVENTS` list and the preload's envelope unwrapping are only exercised in a real run, so a new bridge event must be added to that list by hand.

`tests/scanners/fixtures.ts` provides per-tool store builders rather than JSON blobs — `QoderFx` writes `<sid>.jsonl` plus task JSON and sets ages with `fs.utimesSync`, `HermesFx` and `ZcodeFx` create real SQLite databases with `node:sqlite` from the tools' schemas, `KimiCodeFx` builds the two-level session tree, and `KimiWorkFx` writes the two flat JSON maps with single-sided drops; they are the regression net for the ported scanner semantics and for `collectSessions` skipping a failing tool silently.

The shared search harness lives in the non-spec file `tests/search/harness.ts` so importing it from another spec does not re-run its describes; it supplies a fake `SearchDeps` bundle with a synthetic clock (`now` plus `advance`), recording `search`/`open`/`reveal`, gear-shifting responses (`okPayload`, `goOffline`, `goBroken`, `goRateLimited`) and a `flush()` helper that settles in-flight async work via `setImmediate`.

A repo-wide source-level privacy guard walks every `.ts` file under `src/main` and fails if it contains `GetWindowText` or `window_title`, which is how ADR-0002's "never read window titles" is enforced (by never calling the API, not by filtering afterwards).

An artifact-level privacy guard parses a usage file written by `appendEvent` and asserts the record has exactly the keys `ts` and `exe`, with `start` and `focus` landing in separate per-day JSONL files.

The search chain is guarded twice: a source scan requires `search/engine.ts`, `search/client.ts` and `services/search.ts` to contain no reference to the usage log, no direct disk writes and no hardcoded `http(s)://` URL (the host must come from `BASE_HOST`), and a behaviour-level test runs a full search flow and then reads every file in the usage directory to prove the query word never lands on disk.

Additional surface-specific source guards complement the repo-wide walk: the session-row chain may not read titles through `SendMessageW` nor declare a `title` field on its window-candidate type, and the renderer's plugin loader may not use `require(`/`node:fs` while the preload may not use `node:fs`/`readFileSync`, keeping the renderer's only privileged surface an IPC forwarder.

Kernel-level tests never touch real user data: they create `fs.mkdtempSync` roots and inject the layout-store text, usage directory and config file, with an explicit comment that kernel-level tests must never touch the real `LOCALAPPDATA` file.

Vitest fake timers are the exception rather than the rule and are used only for the Win+D debounce state machine (pure logic over an injected `isDown()` probe), while a service that must be re-imported cleanly is handled with `vi.resetModules()` plus a dynamic import rather than module mocking.
